title: openetl connector descriptor
description: A connector package's version: its metadata, and each role's runtime and spec. `openetl connector package` writes it from openetl-connector.yaml; it isn't written by hand.

metadata.description: Which package and version this is, and what the console shows about it.

name.description: The package: owner/name, or name for the official owner, openetl. Each part is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters.

version.description: Semantic version, without build metadata (`+…`): versions that differ only by it compare as equal.

title.description: A display name, such as PostgreSQL. None: the name.

license.description: An SPDX expression, such as Apache-2.0.

repository.description: The source repository. The package's name stays with it.

docs.description: The package's documentation, which the console's connector catalog links to.

logo.description: An SVG or PNG image, which the UI shows.

author.description: Who makes the package, which the catalog shows.

tags.description: Words the catalog shows with the package, such as database.

release.description: The release the version was built from.

tag.description: The git tag the version was built from.

roles.description: What the package provides: a source, a destination, or both.

ociBlob.description: A blob in an OCI registry, by its digest.

digest.description: A SHA-256 digest: sha256: and 64 hex digits.

duration.description: A Go duration, such as 90s or 15m.

bytes.description: A Kubernetes quantity of bytes, such as 512Mi.

role.description: What a package provides as a source or a destination, and how it runs.

requires.description: What the role needs from the platform.

protocol.description: The connector protocol it speaks; none for a manifest.

features.description: Additions to the protocol after v1 that it can't run without.

platform.description: The oldest openetl release it runs on.

runtime.description: At least one of binaries and an image, or a manifest alone.

binaries.description: One executable per platform, downloaded over HTTP and pinned by digest.

url.description: Where the executable is downloaded from: an http or https URL, or a blob in an OCI registry.

digest.description: The executable's digest. The API fills in a missing one when the version is applied.

image.description: An OCI image index that serves the launch contract under the image contract.

ref.description: A repository, without a tag or digest.

platforms.description: The platforms the index has an image for.

command.description: The connector's argv, where it isn't the entrypoint.

manifest.description: A DeclarativeSource's spec: the role's whole runtime, run in the platform. Sources only.

resources.description: A container launcher's requests and limits, and the job size the role wants.

cpu.description: CPU, as a Kubernetes quantity, such as 500m or 2.

hint.description: The job size a pipeline of this role starts at when it's sized automatically.

state.description: The version of the checkpoint state it writes, and the oldest it reads (at most version).

version.description: The version of the state it writes.

reads.description: The oldest version of the state it can resume from.

egress.description: What the connector means to reach on the network. OpenETL doesn't enforce it yet: connectors are trusted code.

tier.description: `host`: only through the host's services. `proxy`: HTTPS through a forward proxy, to the hosts in `allow`, for vendor SDKs. `raw`: sockets, to the host:port pairs in `allow`, for database drivers.

allow.description: Hosts on the proxy tier, host:port pairs on raw.

acknowledges.description: A source's: it acknowledges upstream once a checkpoint commits.

splits.description: A source's: it divides streams into splits.

resplit.description: A source's: it splits a running split's remainder. Needs splits.

retention.description: A source's: it says, without reading, how much of what it keeps for a pipeline a checkpoint's positions have used.

class.description: How the destination makes an epoch visible. `stage_and_apply`: it stages in `PreCommit` and applies in `Commit`. `transactional_stream`: it flushes into a transaction in `PreCommit` and commits it in `Commit`. `deliver_and_ack`: it delivers during the epoch, and `PreCommit` returns once everything is acknowledged.

scopes.description: The commit scopes a pipeline may choose in `delivery.commit.scope`: `pipeline`, where every stream's epoch becomes visible together, and `stream`, where each stream's does on its own.

dedupeAtApply.description: The destination can skip append and overwrite rows whose `_openetl_id` is already in the target.

defaultCommitInterval.description: The commit interval of a pipeline whose `delivery.commit.interval` sets none.

minCommitInterval.description: The shortest `delivery.commit.interval` a pipeline may set.

maxCommitInterval.description: The longest `delivery.commit.interval` a pipeline may set. None: no maximum.

nanosecondTimestamps.description: Timestamps keep nanoseconds; otherwise only microseconds.

maxIdentifierLength.description: The longest table or column name, in bytes; 0 for no limit.

delivery.description: How epochs reach it: streamed as batches, or staged as Parquet files the platform hands over. None: streamed.

maxWriterLanes.description: The most writer lanes an attempt may open, writing concurrently. None: one.

holds.description: What the destination does with held columns and cells. None: it takes no holds.

byKey.description: Patches a merge stream's rows by their key.

byId.description: Patches an append stream's rows by their `_openetl_id`.

last.description: A held cell can keep the target's value, in a merge stream.

guarded.description: A patch fills a cell only where the target still holds the version it comes from.

config.description: The config's JSON Schema, as Spec returns it.

then.description: A manifest's config and egress are in the manifest, and it speaks no protocol.
